key_concerns: Urban Heat Island intensification in central Ahmedabad (R010 corridor)
Cross-grid pollutant transport from industrial zones (R010_C008 → R010_C009/C010)
Cluster drought pattern affecting 5+ contiguous grids in urban core
Carbon source dominance in built-up zones with limited sink capacity
positive_trends: Peripheral grids (R015_C015, R020_C015) showing improved vegetation health
Rainfall projections suggest monsoon relief in 90-180 day horizon
Carbon sink capacity improving in southern agricultural zones

factors: Industrial zone with highest pollutant concentrations in study area
Near-zero vegetation cover (NDVI 0.06) eliminates natural cooling
Severe drought stress with VHI 0.15 (critical threshold)
Strong carbon source (+0.62) from industrial emissions
Wind-driven pollutant export affecting 2-3 downwind grids
risk_grids.human_summary: This grid represents the most environmentally stressed zone in Ahmedabad. Located in the western industrial belt, it exhibits extreme heat (46°C), virtually no vegetation, severe drought, and the worst air quality. Its pollutants are carried eastward by prevailing winds, degrading neighboring grids R010_C009 and R010_C010.

Carbon source contributing to regional emission load
risk_grids.human_summary: Located in the central urban core, this grid suffers from a triple threat of extreme heat (44.2°C), poor air quality (AQI 285), and severe drought stress (VHI 0.21). It receives windborne pollutants from the industrial R010_C008 to its west. Intervention requires coordinated cross-grid approach.

risk_grids.human_summary: An isolated industrial zone in southeast Ahmedabad showing extreme environmental degradation. Despite being distant from the main urban core, it mirrors the same patterns of extreme heat, negligible vegetation, and severe air quality issues. Its isolation makes it a priority for targeted industrial emission controls and afforestation.
